paragraphs.text: Look After Your Own Car. Tired of paying a garage for jobs you suspect you could manage yourself? This practical eight-week course, led by former mechanic Mateusz Halloran, covers the routine checks every driver should know: tyre pressures and tread, oil and coolant levels, changing a wiper blade and replacing a bulb. In the final two sessions he will show you how to change a wheel safely at the roadside. Classes run on Tuesdays from 7 to 9 p.m. in the workshop behind the main car park, and numbers are limited to ten so that everyone gets hands-on time. Overalls are lent to all students, but you will need to bring your own pair of work gloves and wear sturdy shoes; trainers are not permitted in the workshop. You do not need to bring a car – we use the college's two training vehicles. Fee: £95 (£60 for those over 65).
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Italian for the Holidays. If you are heading to Italy next year and want to do more than point at menus, this relaxed ten-week course is for you. Tutor Rosalind Kwapong, who lived in Bologna for twelve years, focuses on the language you actually need when travelling: ordering food, asking for directions, buying train tickets and making small talk with your hosts. Grammar is kept to a minimum in her classes, and most of each Thursday evening session is spent practising in pairs. The course is aimed at complete beginners. If you studied some Italian at school and are unsure whether the course is right for you, Rosalind is happy to have a short telephone chat with you before you enrol – just leave your number with the college office. The course book is included in the fee of £110, and audio recordings can be downloaded free from the college website.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Real Bread at Home. Learn to bake loaves that put supermarket bread to shame. Over six Wednesday evenings in our newly refurbished teaching kitchen, Noriko Fairweather, who runs her own neighbourhood bakery, will guide you through basic white and wholemeal loaves, flatbreads, bread rolls and, in the final week, a sourdough made from a starter you will take home and keep alive yourself. Everything you bake goes home with you, so bring a large container or cloth bag each week. The course fee of £75 does not cover ingredients; instead, please pay £4 in cash to Noriko at the start of each session. Please note that, although no nuts are used in our recipes, the kitchen is shared with other classes and we cannot guarantee a nut-free environment. Aprons are provided; please tie back long hair.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Get More from Your Phone. Do you own a smartphone or tablet but use it for little more than calls? In this patient, unhurried course, Emeka Castellano and his team of volunteers will show you how to make video calls to family, take and share photographs, shop online safely and spot the warning signs of a scam message. The course runs for five weeks. Sessions take place in the college library on Monday evenings from 6 to 7.30 p.m., slightly earlier than most of our classes, so that learners can travel home before it gets too late. Please bring your own device, fully charged, along with any passwords you already use – written down if necessary. The course is free for anyone who lives in the borough; simply show proof of address, such as a recent utility bill, when you enrol. Others pay £30.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Watercolour for Beginners. Always wanted to paint but never known where to start? Artist Saoirse Patil will share her favourite techniques, from mixing colours and laying a flat wash to painting skies, trees and water. The course lasts eight weeks and meets on Thursday evenings in Studio 3 on the second floor. You will need paper, brushes and a small set of paints. If you would rather not buy these separately, a starter kit containing everything required can be bought from the college reception for £22. At the end of term, students are invited – though not obliged – to show one piece of work in a small exhibition in the college entrance hall. Fee: £85. Places on this popular course fill quickly, so early enrolment is advised.
paragraphs.label: E
